Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 午 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 正中午的大太陽下，積木小隊疊成搖搖晃晃的高塔騎士，拿長紅積木條跟調皮小老鼠的枕頭比劍，兩邊都揮空轉圈，碰一聲撞頭坐倒，掉下來的三根紅積木條和倒下的高塔正好排成「午」，最後兩人握手一起躺下午睡。
object: a squad of interlocking building bricks stacked into a wobbly tower-knight holding a long red brick bar, facing a cheeky cartoon mouse with a pillow under a big noon sun
morph: the head-bonk shakes three red brick bars loose that land as the slanted top stroke, short upper crossbar and long lower crossbar of 午, and the tall brick tower topples and stands upright as the long central vertical stroke
creativeAngle: 改用「友誼比劍」的肢體喜劇：積木小隊疊塔當騎士，老鼠拿枕頭當對手，揮空、轉圈、撞頭的每一步都看得見，而且積木小隊「在最糟時刻倒塌」的特質直接變成午字的長豎。放棄前版日晷影子的靜態變化，詞彙改用午睡，讓決鬥累壞的兩人在中午太陽下倒頭午睡，聲音與畫面同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright cartoon clip on a pale sky-blue background. The only text on screen is one Traditional Chinese glyph 午, formed from solid tomato-red brick bars, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with clear margins. A big friendly yellow noon sun sits at the top edge; every shadow is a tiny dot right under its owner.

0-1.5s: A squad of chunky toy building bricks marches in from the left, click-clacks itself into a tall wobbly tower-knight with two eye-dots and a long red brick bar held like a foam sword. From the right a tiny grey cartoon mouse with huge round ears skids in holding a fluffy pillow, grinning. They square off nose to nose. The voice says the first 午 as the tower leans forward and taps its bar on the ground like a challenge.

1.5-3.5s: The tower winds up with an enormous slow backswing, then swings so hard it whirls in a full circle; the mouse simply steps aside, whiskers twitching. The mouse winds up its pillow with a giant swing, misses completely, and spins like a top too. Both wobble dizzily toward each other, eyes spiraling.

3.5-5s: A frozen half-beat of anticipation, then BOINK: their heads bump with a soft squash-and-stretch bounce and both plop down on their bottoms with dazed grins. The impact shakes three red brick bars loose from the tower: a short slanted bar flips up and lands at the top-left as the leaning first stroke, a short bar settles beneath it as the upper crossbar, and a long bar drops as the wide lower crossbar. The tall brick tower itself topples, bounces once, and stands straight up through the middle as the long central vertical stroke. The voice says the second 午 exactly as the last bar clicks into place and the glyph 午 reads cleanly.

5-8s: The glyph 午 stays perfectly still and fully readable for the final 3 seconds. The reassembled little brick squad and the mouse shake hands in the lower corner, then both give a huge yawn, curl up head to head on the pillow under the noon sun and snooze with small floating sleep-puffs. The voice says 午睡 at the exact moment they flop down to nap. Nothing touches or covers the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 午、午、午睡 (ㄨˇ、ㄨˇ、ㄨˇ ㄕㄨㄟˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single characters, and stops after the word. No other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no English. Soft cartoon pops and a gentle boink only, quieter than the voice. Bright but not neon palette, soft light, no white blowout, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
